legacy_jobs.reason: 22/23 opcodes match target (48/49 bytes); the sole residual is the __loadds prologue's DS source: target loads DS from SS directly ('mov ax,ss; ...; mov ds,ax'), while every isolated compile of this __loadds far pascal callback instead loads a fixed _DATA segment constant ('mov ax, seg _DATA; mov ds,ax'). This matches the well-known LINK.EXE behavior of patching __loadds prologues to 'mov ax,ss' when the module's DGROUP is declared to coincide with the stack segment (STACKSEG DGROUP in the .DEF file) -- a link-time rewrite the compiler itself never emits, so no source-level idiom in an isolated single-function compile can reproduce it. Confirmed across the job's 4 recorded attempts, all converging on the identical single-instruction diff regardless of source shape.
